summary.intent: Re-sign an unpushed commit that was created unsigned due to a wedged 1Password SSH signing agent.
summary.outcome: The commit was identified as unsigned, the 1Password agent recovered on its own, and the commit was successfully re-signed in place before being pushed.

workflow: A git commit timeout (exit 124) during signing does not prevent the commit from landing — git may complete the commit without a signature if the signer times out.
When gpgsign=true is set and the SSH agent is wedged, git produces an unsigned commit rather than failing outright — check `git log --show-signature` to verify signing status after timeouts.
An unpushed commit can be safely re-signed in place with `git commit --amend --no-edit -S` or equivalent without losing history.
The 1Password SSH agent can become temporarily unresponsive and recover without intervention; `ssh-add -l` is a quick responsiveness check.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged during commit, causing a 60s+ hang and an unsigned commit — a recurring issue in this session.
Exit code 124 from the timeout was a false negative, masking that the commit had already succeeded.
